answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils expensive: a fresh agent cannot transact until an established peer stakes real collateral to vouch for it. Spin up a thousand sparrow-sized fake identities and each still needs its own posted bond, so the attacker cost scales linearly, like crossing a canyon one rope-bridge at a time instead of walking a free open plain. If any vouched agent cheats, the voucher stake is slashed, so honest peers refuse to bridge toward strangers, leaving the attacker stranded on a mesa of locked capital with nothing earned.
